newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yakovlev gets order for ten Yak-130 jets.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yakovlev gets order for ten Yak-130 jets.

text.p: Russian plane-maker Yakovlev said on Wednesday that Russia's Defence Ministry has ordered 10 Yak-130 training planes.
A company statement said the planes would be produced at the Sokol aviation plant in Nizhny Novgorod.
"The aircraft will be powered by Russian-Slovak engines and Russian-made avionics," it said.

The statement from Alexander Dondukov, Yakovlev's chief designer, said the Defence Ministry would finance the assembly of the trainer jets. It did not said how much money would be needed to build the planes.
The statement also said that Slovak republic wanted to buy 40 Yak-130s to train its military cadets at all stages, including initial and advanced flight training.

Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev said on Tuesday it would cut its staff of engineers and workers by 25 percent in February. The company had been preparing for the dismissals since the end of last year.
"It will be completed by the end of this month," a Yakovlev official said. It is not clear how many people would be dismissed. The size of the workforce at Yakovlev is a secret.
The official said Yakovlev had encountered serious financial problems because of unpaid debts owed by another aviation plant.
Yakovlev has expressed interest in buying the bankrupt Dutch plane manufacturer Fokker NV, but has so far not received the financial backing to go ahead with a deal.
Yakovlev said it was interested in Fokker to shore up its position in the Russian short-range plane market, of which it wants 25-30 percent by 2000.

Yakovlev used to be the Soviet Union's foremost designer of military aircraft and still designs naval fighter planes. It also designs passenger aircraft and produced the short-range Yak-40 and Yak-42 models.
